result: In 50 ME/CFS vs 50 controls (50% male), plasma lipidomics found lower total PE, arachidonic-PE and hexosylceramides in female patients, and higher HexCer, monounsaturated PE, PI, saturated TG and linoleic-derived oxylipins in male patients; PC/PE/PI/SM-rich components were negatively associated with headache and fatigue severity.
reason: Targeted membrane-phospholipid lipidomics with a sex split fits the PC/SM/ether-lipid finding better than the general claim about metabolome effect size and cross-cohort transfer; small single cohort, so it adds sex-specific detail only.

result: In 116 Berlin ME/CFS patients (no controls), ELISA levels of most adrenergic, muscarinic, ETA/B and AT1 receptor autoantibodies correlated with fatigue and muscle pain in infection-triggered cases; cognitive impairment correlated with AT1-R and ETA-R antibodies, GI symptoms with alpha1/2-AdR antibodies.
reason: Same ELISA GPCR antibodies as Loebel 2015, adding symptom-severity correlations by onset type; there are no controls, so it does not test elevation and does not answer the high-throughput negative. The cohort likely overlaps with Loebel's Berlin cohort.

result: Of 25 newly diagnosed Australian adolescents followed a mean of 2 years (1-5), 65% still met paediatric ME/CFS criteria and 82% self-reported ongoing ME/CFS; fatigue, pain and HRQoL stayed worse than in 23 controls, and baseline pain was associated with persistence (R=0.6, p=0.02).
reason: Measures criteria fulfilment and recovery over follow-up in an adolescent subgroup; it is small, but it sits uneasily with the finding's unchecked note that adolescents have a better prognosis.

result: Fine mapping (5 more classical HLA loci, 5,342 SNPs) in 427 Norwegian CCC cases vs 480 controls found two independent signals: rs4711249 in class I (spanning DDR1/GTF2H4/VARS2/SFTA2/DPCR1) and rs9275582 in class II, with the class II signal most likely at HLA-DQB1 amino-acid position 57.
reason: Same Norwegian case cohort as Lande 2020 (not independent, and a 2021 paper, so not already cited); fine mapping refines the Lande HLA-DQB1 signal, but it is a small control set and adds no replication against DecodeME.

result: Six years after the 2005 Jena outbreak, 80 serologically confirmed Q fever cases and 52 seronegative household members did not differ on the CDC symptom inventory or on CFS criteria (3.8% vs 3.8%, p=0.655), and no one had chronic Q fever.
reason: Directly tests the rate of persistent post-Q-fever fatigue syndrome and finds no excess over household controls, against the ~20% and long-persistence claim; small cohort with self-selected participants (80 of 331 cases).

result: In an online survey of 3,762 people with confirmed or suspected long COVID from 56 countries, fatigue, PEM and cognitive dysfunction were the most frequent symptoms after month 6, 85.9% had relapses triggered mainly by exercise, physical or mental activity and stress, and over 91% had not recovered by 35 weeks.
reason: Reports how common PEM and exertion-triggered relapse are in long COVID; it does not measure PEM onset delay, duration or recovery time after exertion, so it does not fit the timing finding.

result: Targeted and untargeted metabolomics (888 analytes) in 106 ME/CFS cases vs 91 controls found lower plasmalogens, PCs, sphingomyelins, choline, ceramides and carnitines, higher long-chain TGs and dicarboxylic acids, and female classification AUC 0.794.
reason: already cited: this is the preprint of Che 2022 (same 106/91 cohort and plasmalogen/CDP-choline findings), which is in finding_studies.

result: In 213 adults with long COVID (85.5% women, 72.3% ill for at least 6 months) in an online survey, mean FACIT-F was 18±10, 71.4% had chronic fatigue, and 58.7% met the DSQ-PEM scoring thresholds used in ME/CFS.
reason: Measures PEM prevalence in long COVID with the DSQ-PEM, not PEM onset delay, duration or recovery time; small self-selected survey.

result: Among 70 previously hospitalised COVID-19 survivors, the 41 with persistent dyspnoea had lower percent-predicted peak VO2 (77.8 vs 99) than the 29 asymptomatic survivors, with normal echo and lung function but higher VE/VCO2 slope (32 vs 29.4, p=0.022) and lower PetCO2 (34.5 vs 38, p=0.025).
reason: Symptomatic vs recovered survivors show lower peak VO2 with no cardiac limit; it adds a ventilatory-inefficiency pattern. Small, single-centre and mainly hospitalised cohort. The screen summary wrongly said PetCO2 was higher; it was lower.

result: In dyspnoeic vs asymptomatic post-COVID survivors, CPET showed a higher VE/VCO2 slope (32 vs 29.4, p=0.022) and lower PetCO2 (34.5 vs 38 mmHg, p=0.025), which the authors read as V/Q mismatch or hyperventilation syndrome.
reason: Measures exercise hyperventilation and low end-tidal CO2, not orthostatic hypocapnia or cerebral blood flow on tilt; this fits the exercise hyperventilation part of vascular-hypocapnia, as a long COVID version.
